title: Understanding MSE on Test Data
text: Mean Squared Error (MSE) on held-out test data measures how well the model generalizes to unseen data. Consider how removing a feature might affect this generalization.

title: Effect of Removing a Feature
text: Removing a feature can reduce model complexity, which might decrease variance but increase bias. Consider how these changes might affect the MSE on test data.

title: Bias-Variance Tradeoff
text: The bias-variance tradeoff is crucial in understanding the effects on MSE. Removing a feature might increase bias but decrease variance. How does this tradeoff affect the MSE on test data?

title: Analyzing Effects on MSE
text: Consider both possible outcomes: Removing a feature might lead to an increase in bias, potentially increasing MSE, but it might also reduce variance, potentially decreasing MSE. What are the possible effects?
